cases.customer_question: Can a product that only implements BR/EDR pairing be qualified as a BR/EDR-only Bluetooth product under the current Bluetooth SIG qualification system?
question_variants: Can we register only BR/EDR without BLE?
Is BR/EDR-only qualification still possible after the 2024 qualification system update?
Can a product disable BLE functionality but still reference a BR/EDR/LE stack?
Why does consistency check fail when removing LE layers?
Can a Classic-only product reuse a dual-mode QDID?
Do we need RF PHY testing if BLE is not implemented in the product?
cases.actual_issue: The customer wanted to qualify a product that operationally uses only BR/EDR pairing while reusing existing BR/EDR/LE controller and host stack qualified designs. The newer Qualification Workspace consistency rules created invalid ICS dependencies when attempting to remove LE-related layers from a reused dual-mode design.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The Bluetooth SIG qualification system became stricter after the 2024 Qualification Workspace update. If a reused controller or host stack was originally qualified as BR/EDR/LE dual-mode, removing LE layers often causes consistency-check errors because shared protocol layers depend on both BR/EDR and LE lower layers. In practice, many products that only use Classic Bluetooth behavior are still registered as dual-mode products while simply not exposing BLE features in the final product behavior.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that after the 2024-07-01 Qualification Workspace update, dual-mode referenced designs generally must remain dual-mode because consistency checks enforce inter-layer dependencies between GAP, L2CAP, LL, and LMP layers. Attempting to delete LE-related lower layers from a reused BR/EDR/LE qualified design causes Invalid results during consistency checking. Although a theoretical path exists to create a true BR/EDR-only registration by performing new protocol-layer testing and rebuilding stack evidence, this is impractical for most product makers because the required protocol-layer source access and testing would require cooperation from the stack vendor and could cost approximately 2-3 million JPY. The consultant recommended using the existing dual-mode controller and host stack registrations unchanged through the Combine Unmodified Design process while implementing only BR/EDR pairing behavior in the final product.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification Workspace consistency rules require inter-layer dependencies to remain valid. Shared upper layers such as GAP and L2CAP depend on both BR/EDR and LE lower-layer structures in reused dual-mode designs. Reusing an existing dual-mode QDID without modification avoids triggering new protocol testing requirements and Invalid consistency results.
cases.final_recommendation: Reuse the existing BR/EDR/LE controller and host stack qualified designs through the Combine Unmodified Design process, keep the qualification dual-mode, and limit the shipped product behavior to BR/EDR pairing only without enabling BLE advertising or scanning.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: If LE layers are improperly removed from a reused dual-mode design, the Qualification Workspace consistency check can generate Invalid errors and potentially trigger extensive Core-layer testing requirements. The consultant warned that attempting to rebuild compliant BR/EDR-only stack evidence could become unrealistic in both schedule and cost, with possible additional testing costs of approximately 2-3 million JPY.
